559.caption: The email caption read: “I fear the Pandemic Beard, already at full Hemingway, will reach full Johannes Brahms before we have a vaccine.”

560.caption: After he sold Bosenbüttel, Fritz Mueller moved most of his money to America through Bremen banks. He kept some of it in gold coins, which he put into this money belt that Johanne wore on the emigration to Indiana.

562.caption: Thomas and James love their cornbread and prefer the kitchen to the dining room for their breakfast. With neither table nor chairs, seating is where you find it.

563.caption: Archie loves his school, Covid precautions and all.

565.caption: With the new, larger family settled in at 101 Prospect Park SW, Archie began reading books to his 9-day-old sister.

571.caption: Thomas and James found puddles everywhere after a whole morning of rain in January 2021. Puddles, of course, are perfect for punschering.

572.caption: Dinosaurs of all kinds and sizes were a big hit when they arrived from Great-uncle Binyon and Great-aunt Ting. The triceratops prefers banana slices.

573.caption: Leia Reva Nickel arrived in Brooklyn on Thursday, December 10, 2020. She checked in at 7 pounds, 11 ounces, and 20.5 inches.

574.caption: Leia slipped right into the family routine with Mom, Dad, and Big Brother Archie.

575.caption: At home on Mom’s lap, comfy, fed, and not a care in the world.

576.caption: Leia just about a month old: Alert, eyes tracking movement, happy.

577.caption: Thursday, January 21 – about five weeks old.

579.caption: Archie, lover of all things pasta, enjoyed his first encounter with the famous German noodle, part of a holiday care package from Binyon and Ting.

580.caption: Snow arrived in Richmond Sunday, January 31, 2021. Heavy, wet, ideal for snowballs and snowman-making — and a perfect way to celebrate Dad’s birthday.

581.caption: Unfamiliar stuff, this snow. Rare in Richmond, it may have been James’s first encounter with a Minnesota-style winter.

582.caption: Big Brother Archie brought out some of his most prized possessions — especially bears and wubs — for Little Sister Leia to explore.

583.caption: Erich E.A. Mueller and Maria Carolina Bergt, seated, with their nine children. Rear, from left: Gustav, Martha, Adolf, Theodora. Front, from left: Gerhard, Emma, Louisa (in white), Magdalene, Elizabeth.

584.caption: Leia is just about two months old.

585.caption: A charcoal sketch, possibly created by his son Fritz Mueller, appeared on a Family Search website in 2018. A note on the back says “by FGW Mueller” and has the date as 1865. It may have been handed down by Gertrude Mueller Rehwinkel.

587.caption: On the last night of Opa and Oma’s visit to Richmond, there was a grand fire in the fire pit and hamburgers for supper. A beautiful night.

588.caption: James and Oma spent a long time examining and playing with the tiny Red Car. Like Great Uncle Tim with “Bearsie,” James could not sleep without it and was very sad. In the morning after a night when no one could find it, James’s Mom drove to Target and bought four of them.

589.caption: Georg Mueller owned this tobacco box late in the 18th century. He gave it to his son Fritz, who took it along when he and his family emigrated to Kendallville, Indiana, in 1865.

591.caption: Peter, proud father, holds Daniel January 30, 1982, two days after Dan’s birth.

592.caption: Esther and Bill Crawley in an undated Polaroid likely taken in the summer of 1982.

593.caption: Mary and Friedrich C.J. were married in 1876. In 1890, five years after elder brother Wilhelm had left farming, Mary and Friedrich owned clear title to the 108-acre Mueller farm.

601.caption: His dad actually made it, but Archie was on hand to help deliver chocolate malts to the cousins at Oma and Opa’s house.

606.caption: Archie was fascinated with washers, dryers, and the whole laundry process. Tom was amazed at the changing words and numbers on the display. James was just happy to be there.

607.caption: James pitched in on the sour cherry harvest during an early July visit with his family. His pickings helped make nine jars of cherry jam.

608.caption: Thomas helped pick sour cherries in early July 2021. He turned out to be pretty good at it and helped squish out the pits.

609.caption: Anson spent a few days and nights as a research subject in Mary Carskadon’s Butler Hospital sleep lab, all wired up to record brain activity. A grad student TA shot the Polaroid.

610.caption: Archie yanked the beets out of the garden soil. Anson and Archie washed them with garden spritzer (on a hot day). Opa cooked them. Leia ate them by the handful and enjoyed herself immensely.

611.caption: Archie, Anson, and Opa were the first visitors of the day at the Norman Bird Sanctuary. Three large deer bounded across the trail. There were turtles on the rocks, lots of bird sounds, and many trails.

612.caption: Danny and Susie were part of the wedding ceremony, each receiving an engraved small silver plate. Uncle Tim, the best man, had a pocket full of gummi bears just in case.

613.caption: First day of preschool, 2021 — a very happy time.

614.caption: Leia appears to be lending a hand during a family hunt for Honeycrisps, Galas, and Fujis in a New Jersey orchard. They picked plenty — enough for a homemade apple tart.

616.caption: Dan and Aliki were married on the terraza of Aliki’s house in Agios Lavrentios.

621.caption: Nimble and lightweight, 11-year-old Anson plunged fearlessly down the double-black-diamond trails. His somewhat larger, self-taught father stuck to the greens and a few of the blues.

622.caption: Doing his part to celebrate the victory of light over darkness, Archie enjoyed his first experience with live fireworks.

623.caption: Thomas, 5, in his first year of “real” school. He loves it.

625.caption: In the spring of 1995, Mom and the three kids visited Nana and Grampa in Arizona. (Dad had to be in Washington to run a press conference.) Anson, 8 years old, filled him in on the visit.

626.caption: Walter and Elsie Melahn managed to tame a deer at their resort on Lake George, Minnesota. Bucky was supposed to be a great favorite for guests who had kids. Mark wasn’t so sure.

627.caption: There's a lot to see and do in a mirror. Leia preferred to look straight at the camera ... or its reflection.

628.caption: Oma and Leia had lots of time to get acquainted sitting on the “plop couch,” a favorite piece of family room furniture.

629.caption: Leia’s great-great-uncle Gerhard once remarked that sleeping infants “are in cahoots with the angels.”

630.caption: During a four-grandchild visit to Oma and Opa’s house, Archie helped bring in the 2021 sour cherry harvest, much of which Opa turned into jam. Squeezing out the pits was the best part.

631.caption: The snowblower did the heavy lifting but there was still lots left to do.

632.caption: Leia tried out the child’s chair great-uncle Jim made in 1989 for his niece Ashley, now in her 30s. The maquette-scale piece is styled after *Three Chairs for Queens College,* a large sculptural work installed on the Queens College campus in October 1984.

633.caption: At 14 months, Leia uses her spoon to get drippy tomato soup from the bowl to her mouth. A healthy portion made the trip successfully.

634.caption: Mark was born on election day, November 2, 1948. It’s possible, though highly unlikely, that the birth announcement ran in this next-day iconic edition of the *Chicago Tribune.* (The morning *Washington Post* was not much better. Under the headline “Truman’s Defeat by Wide Margin Seen,” the *Post* said “Gov. Thomas E. Dewey of New York ... is regarded as a certain winner over President Truman. ... Should it turn out otherwise, the polltakers and prognosticators would be forced into the greatest crow-eating debacle in the annals of American politics.”)

636.caption: Leia inherited Great-uncle Jim’s *Child’s Chair,* a toddler-scale rendering of a much larger work. It turned out to be great for climbing onto, jumping off of, and even sitting in.

638.caption: Leia discovered her great-grandmother’s Steinway on a visit to Opa and Oma’s house in late May. She seemed to like the bass notes best.

639.caption: Doug loved the design and performance of the Datson Z but disliked the color choices. Then in 1976 the Datsun 280Z appeared in British Racing Green.

640.caption: Doug, Ann, and the 1976 British Racing Green Datson 280Z, heading out for an evening at the “Fall Brawl.” Everything turned out well — even for the car.

643.caption: It was a little breezy, but we wanted to try out the “Studebaker” on the sand. It was a tough pull except for the smooth, wet sand at the water's edge. The all-terrain wheelchair was a birthday gift from Alli’s siblings.

645.caption: Opa Mueller, twice disappointed and not subtle about it, finally had a son on December 4, 1904. Oma had little Gerhard’s photo taken for Opa’s birthday, but the surprise was ruined when another customer met Opa on the street and said, “I see your boy had his picture taken in his rubber boots.”

647.caption: A soothing session in the rocking chair was a grand success when Thomas and his parents came for a visit in August 2018.

658.caption: Thanksgiving marks the start of the *Stollen* season, which makes the bedtime snack special. By the time the whole household had retired, half the first loaf was gone.

659.caption: Leia turned two on a Saturday morning with cupcakes and friends.

661.caption: Olivia did her part as the new three-member family began life together and a new and different household began to emerge.

662.caption: After a couple nights at the hospital, newborn Olivia moved into her newly outfitted nursery on the first floor of her parents’ apartment. Everyone was very happy, very healthy, very tired.

710.caption: Gerhard's living siblings arrived in Height of Land for his funeral. From left: Herbert, Ernst, Frieda, Adelheid, and Kurt.

908.caption: *Fritz Müllers Reise nach Amerika* was published in two installments by the *Jugend-Blätter,* a monthly magazine for young German readers. Issues from 1867 were collated and sold in book form, a copy of which resides in the Lilly Library at the University of Indiana.

3070.caption: Michael, Wilhelmina, and the infant Albert Nickel, listed on the SS Lessing's passenger manifest, arriving in New York on May 7, 1879.

3071.caption: Michael, Wilhelmina, and Albert Nickel, sometime after the family settled in Milwaukee.
